items.question: What condition must an integer $p > 1$ satisfy to be classified as a prime number?
items.answer: An integer $p > 1$ is classified as a prime number if its only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$.

items.question: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic regarding the prime factorization of an integer $n > 1$.
items.answer: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every integer $n > 1$ can be represented as a unique product of prime numbers, up to the order of factors: $n = p_1^{e_1} p_2^{e_2} \cdots p_k^{e_k}$.

items.question: What condition defines two integers $a$ and $b$ as being coprime?
items.answer: Two integers $a$ and $b$ are coprime (or relatively prime) if their greatest common divisor is $1$, written as $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.

items.question: According to the Division Algorithm, what is the exact range of conditions required for the remainder $r$ when dividing integer $a$ by positive integer $b$?
items.answer: According to the Division Algorithm, the remainder $r$ must be a non-negative integer strictly less than $b$, satisfying the condition $0 \le r < b$.
